svg.title: Diagram of what USPS pages say about a Return Receipt. What it shows: the recipient's signature, the date of delivery and the actual delivery address if different. Bought at the time of mailing; it cannot be bought after mailing. Green card, PS Form 3811: mailed to the sender after delivery; the form is attached at mailing and the mail is endorsed Return Receipt Requested; the card cannot be viewed online. Electronic: bought at a Post Office, then requested on the USPS Tracking website with an email address; usually available within 48 hours of delivery; kept two years. If it did not arrive: ask for the delivery record within 90 days of purchase with PS Form 3811-A. The pages differ on when the email should arrive, on how the email address is given and on the refund timing.
svg.text: USPS Return Receipt
What the USPS pages say
1. What it shows
The recipient's signature, the date of
delivery and the actual delivery address
if it differs. Bought at the time of
mailing; it cannot be bought after.
2. Green card (PS Form 3811)
Attached at mailing; the mail is endorsed
"Return Receipt Requested." Mailed to the
sender after delivery. Cannot be viewed
online. The Related Tracking Number
tracks the card, not the mailpiece.
3. Electronic
Bought at a Post Office, not on USPS.com.
Requested on USPS Tracking with the
article number and an email address.
Usually available within 48 hours of
delivery. Kept two years. Courts decide
its legal status.
4. If it did not arrive
Ask for the delivery record within 90
days of purchase: PS Form 3811-A at a
Post Office, with your receipt. The fee
is refunded only if USPS fails to
provide the signature.
Where the pages differ
Email timing: within 48 hours of delivery
(Electronic FAQ) or check at 3 to 5 days
(Basics FAQ). Email choice: the Basics FAQ,
the DMM and the Electronic FAQ describe
it differently. Refund timing: two
wordings that the pages do not reconcile.
Sources: USPS FAQs 000006076, 000007257;
DMM 503 section 6.0; read Nov. 24, 2026
